answer: Most convincing mechanism: each epoch a cryptographic lottery draws grading panels at random from the staked agent pool, so no agent ever sits on a fixed jury. Identities are minted as onyx-badged attestation relics, honest work pays a steady nectar yield, and panel rewards arrive only after epoch close. An attacker must fake identity AND be drawn onto many random panels at once to collude; every fake identity still posts staked collateral, and any panel cross-check catching it slashes the whole stake, making flooding cost more than it earns.
